newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

SUGAR: World market for September 19 - White sugar futures in London ended firmer on short-covering. December added $3.20 to close at $331.50 while March was up $2.10 also at $331.50. There was little fundamental news to give the market direction.

In New York raw sugar futures finished a narrowly traded session firmer as prices continued to consolidate after the recent sell-off. October closed 2 points higher at 11.42 cents/lb while March added 7 points to close at 11.37 cents/lb. The October/March spread fell to 5 points compared with 10 points the previous day. The spread could narrow further due to increasing availabilities of new crop sugar.

C.CZARNIKOW - According to London trade house C.Czarnikow sugar production in the north/northeast of Brazil in 1996/97 could exceed last year's record of 3.54 million tonnes, raw value. Czarnikow said that although no progress has yet been reported, early indications continue to bear out previous expectations that the new crop will be a very good one.

It added that the Brazilian government was still hesitating to remove a 40 per cent tax on the remaining 20 per cent of sugar set for export in this year's crop plan. But NNE exports could soar once the tax was removed, as it already has been for most of the 1996/97 crop, it said.

HONG KONG - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 19,094 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 18,493 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) up to 141,668 tonnes against 139,778 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 237,332 tonnes against 208,640 tonnes in 1994.

Major countries of origin in January/July 1996 were South Korea with 66,598 tonnes whites against 68,982 tonnes, Australia with 16,476 tonnes, up from 11,391 tonnes and the United Kingdom with 14,039 tonnes compared to 15,478 tonnes.

Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 3,525 tonnes, which brought cumulative exports in January/July up to 42,576 tonnes against 39,023 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 reached 67,970 tonnes compared to 42,696 tonnes in 1994.
The major country of destination in January/July 1996 was China with 28,100 tonnes whites compared to 18,548 tonnes and 11,964 tonnes raws against 1,601 tonnes.

BELGIUM - Sugar imports in April 1996 amounted to 66,445 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 80,258 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1995/96 (October/April) up to 570,094 tonnes against 750,928 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.14 million tonnes compared to 663,985 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in October/April 1995/96 were France with 428,288 tonnes whites against 609,251 tonnes, the Netherlands with 46,922 tonnes compared to 9,394 tonnes and Germany with 42,773 tonnes, down from 64,398 tonnes.

Sugar exports in April 1996 reached 54,688 tonnes, down from 119,550 tonnes exported in April 1995. This brought cumulative exports in the first seven months of 1995/96 (October/April) up to 771,380 tonnes against 950,839 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.57 million tonnes, up from 1.34 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/April 1995/96 were Syria with 127,496 tonnes whites against 93,186 tonnes, Israel with 84,765 tonnes, up from 60,886 tonnes, Turkey with 84,451 tonnes against 31,772 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 53,858 tonnes against 153,847 tonnes.

EU - The European Union beet sugar output is expected to total 15.42 million tonnes, white value, in 1996/97 (July/June), compared with the July forecast of 15.71 million and last year's production of 15.64 million, according to an official forecast. The forecast was based on an average yield of 7.65 tonnes per ha and an area of 2.01 million ha, a trade source said.
A Commission official cautioned that the crop forecast is provisional and likely to change once the harvest was completed. Sowings were slightly below the 2.09 million ha sown in 1995/96.
